title: ARMS technique choreography class / Tribal Fusion Bellydance / by Olga Meos

method.teacher_system: The teacher introduces a warm-up sequence for arms and wrists while seated on the floor, breaking down each stretch and movement step-by-step. She then integrates upper body articulation and core engagement before progressing into arm choreography and full combinations.

practices.what: Sit comfortably on the floor and practice making horizontal circles with your chest.
Place arms in front, stretch down, and then roll up while performing shoulder circles back.
Lower and raise your head in sync with shoulder circles, making slow circles with both.
Change the direction of the shoulder and head circles slowly and smoothly.
Place hands behind your head and gently stretch side to side, then add front and side movements.
Place one arm behind your head, slide to the side, and feel the stretch along your obliques.
Extend your elbow in a diagonal line and gently twist your upper body upward.
Hold your arms in front of you and make faster circles outward, then change direction.
Keep both arms moving in the same direction in circles, then speed up as much as you can.
Clasp your hands together in front and make large circular rotations with your wrists forward.

adaptations.difficulty: Having hip or knee discomfort while sitting cross-legged on the floor
adaptations.adjustment: Place a yoga block under your hips to make the seated position more comfortable.

adaptations.difficulty: Having knee pain or feeling restricted on the floor
adaptations.adjustment: Place your hips on a chair and do the stretching and warm-up there.

adaptations.difficulty: Feeling uncomfortable in the seated posture
adaptations.adjustment: Use a block or any pillow underneath to lift yourself higher.

adaptations.difficulty: Finding floor sitting difficult for mobility
adaptations.adjustment: Sit on a chair so that it is more comfortable to work.

beliefs.belief: The teacher believes the learner is already a dancer who can add their own style to the movements.
The teacher believes in the learner's ability to do something amazing.
The teacher believes that creativity, isolation, and layering are key to learning dance.

feelings.response: The teacher suggests using a prop to make the position more comfortable.
The teacher suggests an alternative, like sitting on a chair, to make the position more comfortable.
The teacher acknowledges the difficulty and encourages the learner to keep trying.

moments.says: The teacher welcomes the learner to a new tutorial video about arm technique and a combo, and mentions a surprise.
The teacher announces a prize for the dancer who learns the choreography and adds their own style.
The teacher offers the learner the option to use a yoga block or a pillow under their hips to make the position more comfortable.
The teacher normalizes the difficulty of the pose by saying not everyone has mobile knees and suggests sitting on a chair instead.
The teacher acknowledges that changing the direction of the arm rotation is difficult to understand, but encourages the learner to keep trying.
The teacher reassures the learner that it is normal for one side to feel better than the other.

mentor.what_stays: The teacher leaves the learner feeling capable of dancing and confident in their own style.
